direct_conflicts.description: cross-merchant, perma-bull, vol-convexity expect NZD higher while dollar-king, perma-bear, trend-follower expect NZD lower

conflict_synopsis.core_view: AUDNZD at a 5y extreme prices AU outperformance that housing, cooler inflation and softer activity do not support versus NZ, and USD pairs contaminate that gap.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: AU housing/financial-conditions confirmation versus NZ activity/inflation follow-through after the GDP beat and India FTA.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AU housing stabilizes versus NZ, or NZ labor deterioration plus unobserved NZ yield premium justifies the AUDNZD extreme.

contribution.stance_summary: USD pairs mix a common post-FOMC tightening bid into otherwise distinct AU-NZ differentials. Short AUDNZD spot isolates Australian housing/financial-conditions damage against New Zealand's hotter inflation, firmer activity and GDP beat without owning the dollar.

catalysts: Further Australian housing/financial-conditions prints confirming the RBA tightening channel.
NZ activity/inflation follow-through after the Q2 GDP beat and India FTA implementation.
Any fade in the common USD tightening bid that currently masks NZDUSD cheapness and leaves AUDNZD as the residual.
evidence_refs: rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
rollup:New Zealand Q2 GDP slows to 0.2% q/q but beats forecasts

expression_comparison.rationale: Dedicated spot-FX seat. The intended discrepancy is an AU-versus-NZ relative-value gap in currency space. Official NZ sovereign yields are unavailable in this packet, so AU-NZ rate RV, AUDNZD carry, and the AUDNZD~AU-NZ_2Y screen cannot be formed. Short AUDUSD or long NZDUSD would import the common USD tightening factor after the Fed hike; short AUDCAD fights a measured +165bp 2Y AUD-over-CAD carry that can justify that cross's richness. AUDNZD is the cleaner isolation.

trade.invalidation: Thesis fails if AU housing and activity stabilize or rebound relative to NZ while NZ labor deterioration (unemployment already 5.6%) and missing NZ yield information resolve as a large, persistent AUD carry premium that can justify the 5y AUDNZD extreme. A 1d extension is not itself invalidation; a regime in which AUDUSD, not the cross, becomes the stretching leg would mean USD is the true driver and this expression no longer owns the gap.
trade.mispricing: AUDNZD is at a 5y extreme (z 3.12) while AUDUSD is not. Pricing implies AU outperformance versus NZ that is not supported by cooler AU inflation (49.2 vs 51.6), weaker AU activity (49.2 vs 52.0), or the RBA housing channel versus NZ's GDP beat and FTA. USD expressions bury that gap inside Fed/USD beta. AUDCAD richness has a documented carry explanation; AUDNZD richness does not, because NZ yields are missing rather than because a measured NZ rate discount justifies the cross.
principal_risks: NZ labor is already the softer of the two (score 47.0; unemployment 5.6%); a labor-led NZ slowdown can keep NZD the funding/weak leg.
Official NZ yields are unavailable, so the trade may be fighting unobserved AUDNZD carry; that is a known gap, not a measured tailwind.
Positioning/flow is unavailable; a crowded short-NZD or CTA trend in AUDNZD can extend a 5y extreme.
Global energy/tightening shock can keep both commodity currencies offered, with NZD remaining the higher-beta underperformer.
No executable broker prices; ECB fixings are research/reference only.
trade.thesis: FACT: ECB same-fixing AUDNZD is at 1.2468 on 2026-09-18, 99.96th percentile of the 5y window, z_5y 3.12, +4.27% over 1m and +0.65% on the day. AUDUSD is only 84.3rd percentile 5y (z 1.23, +0.20% 1m). NZDUSD is 8.6th percentile 5y (z -1.15, -3.90% 1m). Decomposition: the 1m AUDNZD rally is NZD underperformance versus a still-bid dollar, not independent AUD strength. AU temperature: inflation 49.2, labor 47.8, activity 49.2, consumer 51.0. NZ temperature: inflation 51.6, labor 47.0, activity 52.0, consumer 48.5. AU 2Y 4.999% and 10Y 5.348% sit at the 99th percentile of their 1y windows, with housing evidence that NSW stamp-duty receipts fell 24% y/y in August, transactions fell 18%, and Sydney/Melbourne values are more than 7% below peak. NZ Q2 GDP printed 0.2% q/q but beat forecasts; NZ parliament passed an India FTA covering about 95% of NZ exports. Desk thesis: energy shock and Fed/BoJ/BoE tightening are a common G10 duration/USD factor. INFERENCE: market pricing of AUDNZD as a 5y extreme requires Australia to remain the relatively stronger Pacific commodity currency, which is the opposite of the housing-versus-activity/inflation split. Expressing AU housing damage in AUDUSD shorts the dollar's post-hike bid; expressing NZ cheapness in NZDUSD does the same in reverse. Short AUDNZD owns the bilateral gap and nets out USD. AUDCAD is also 99.96th percentile 5y (z 2.76) but is co-explained by a live +165bp 2Y yield gap and only +1.95% 1m, so it is the inferior fade. UNKNOWN: NZ 2Y/5Y/10Y, AUDNZD carry, positioning/flow, and executable broker levels. NZ labor is a live offset (unemployment 5.6%).
why_now: AUDNZD printed a 5y extreme on the cutoff date (99.96th percentile, z 3.12) with a 1m move of +4.27% and a 1d extension of +0.65%, so the dislocation is live rather than stale.

Australian housing evidence from 16 Sep shows the RBA tightening channel already biting (stamp duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, prices >7% off peak) while NZ Q2 GDP beat and an India FTA passed in the same window.
The Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, BoJ hike to 1.25%, and hawkish BoE hold make USD the common factor; waiting to express AU-NZ via AUDUSD or NZDUSD now maximally contaminates the view.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Post-hike US 2s10s flattening prices a growth scare that hard activity, tight credit and low vol do not confirm, so the curve should steepen.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Expansionary US activity/labor prints after a fully priced 25bp hike, against a 1y-extreme 25bp 2s10s.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Labor and surveys break weaker with HY/VIX stress while 2s10s keeps flattening.

contribution.stance_summary: Post-hike recession flattening is over-discounted: hard activity, credit and vol still look expansionary, so the cleanest pro-growth expression is a duration-neutral US 2s10s steepener rather than stretched cyclical FX.

catalysts: US activity and labor prints that stay expansionary versus a curve that already flattened 21bp in a month
August retail +1.2% feeding into spending and reducing the consumer-scare read from Michigan 47.8
Canada activity/energy pass-through keeping North American term premium from collapsing even if the Fed is done for this meeting
NZ GDP beat and India FTA as global cyclical confirmation, expressed here via the US curve rather than NZD because NZ yields are unavailable
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
rollup:New Zealand Q2 GDP slows to 0.2% q/q but beats forecasts
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Duration-neutral US 2s10s steepener: receive UST 2Y versus pay UST 10Y. Packet print is 25bp on 2026-09-18, 1y percentile 0.2% / z_1y -2.45 after a -21bp 1m flatten (z -2.20). Alternative considered: long CA-US 5Y (pay CA 5Y / receive US 5Y) at -124bp, 1y percentile 0.2% and 5y percentile 6.9%.
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates are preferred because the growth-versus-recession discrepancy lives in curve shape, not in a cheap FX level. US 2s10s owns that gap directly after a fully priced 25bp hike, while NZDUSD mixes an energy-importer shock, unavailable NZ yields, and weak NZ labor (47.0). USDCAD is inferior because the packet's USDCAD vs CA-US 2Y residual is weak (r-squared 0.022) and 140bp 2Y carry favors USD over CAD. CA-US 5Y is a strong RV but is closer to the existing 150-175bp policy-rate gap (Fed 3.75-4.00% vs BoC 2.25%) than to a growth mispricing. NZ-involved rate RV is unavailable.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long NZDUSD (spot 0.5711, 5y percentile 8.6%, -3.90% 1m) as the cheapest cyclical USD pair after NZ Q2 GDP +0.2% q/q beat forecasts; runner-up short USDCAD on Canada activity 53.2 versus US 49.92.

trade.horizon: 4-8 weeks; post-hike data and next inflation/labor prints to test whether the 1m flatten was a growth scare or a completed hiking event
trade.invalidation: ISM Services or manufacturing fall into contraction, payrolls and unemployment break materially weaker, and HY OAS/VIX reprice a growth accident while 2s10s keeps flattening. A 5y-window confirmation that 25bp is a normal curve in this hiking regime without a growth rebound would also downgrade the stretch argument.
trade.mispricing: US 2s10s at 25bp (1y percentile 0.2%, 1m -21bp) prices a hiking-into-slowdown path that is not confirmed by expansionary ISM services, stable labor, tight HY, low VIX, or high copper. The 5y 2s10s percentile of 54% means this is a change/1y-distribution discrepancy, not a 5y cheapness claim. Credit-equity-survey triangulation says the recession flattening overshot.
principal_risks: Energy shock absorbers weaken further and a genuine stagflation hit validates the flatten; BoC already flags fuel pass-through and Shell/Equinor warn buffers are thinner.
US consumer remains the soft spot: temperature 48.5, Michigan preliminary September 47.8 (-7.5% m/m), Q2 GDP +1.5% SAAR versus +2.1% in Q1.
The 5y 2s10s percentile is 54%, so 1y-window extremes can persist if this hiking regime has a lower curve mean; mean reversion is a yardstick, not the signal.
Another hawkish Fed or upside CPI surprise can extend bear-flattening if 2Y cheapens faster than 10Y; August CPI already kept the tightening bias intact.

Australian housing (stamp duty -24% y/y, prices more than 7% off peak) is a real regional growth hole; this trade does not own that, but a broader commodity risk-off could still flatten UST via a global scare.
Positioning, dealer balance sheet and executable levels are unknown; paper books are empty and Cot/flow is a known gap.
trade.structure: Duration-neutral 2s10s steepener: receive US 2Y versus pay US 10Y. Equal-yield weights are not claimed; packet notes 2s5s10s is equal-yield, not DV01-neutral. No executable structure or size is in the packet.
trade.thesis: FACT: The Fed delivered the widely priced 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%; futures had assigned greater than 90% odds before the meeting. US 2Y is 4.76% (1y percentile 99.8%, +57bp 1m) and US 10Y is 5.01% (1y percentile 99.6%, +36bp 1m), leaving 2s10s at 25bp. That spread's 252-observation percentile is 0.0 with z -2.49, 1y percentile 0.2% / z_1y -2.45, and a -21bp 1m change (z -2.20); 5s10s is 15bp with 1y percentile 0.4%. FACT: Hard US data are not collapsing. Unemployment is 4.1% unchanged; payrolls +162k with positive revisions; ISM Services 55.4 with business activity and new orders above 60; ISM Manufacturing 54.6 still expansionary; August retail sales +1.2% m/m after July was revised to -0.5%. FACT: Risk markets are not pricing a growth accident: VIX 15.44 (14.7th percentile), HY OAS 270bp (13.7th percentile), S&P 500 7638 (90th percentile, +1.13% 1d), copper 6.59 (92nd percentile). Canada Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q and activity temperature 53.2 are the strongest cyclical prints in the four-country set; NZ Q2 GDP +0.2% q/q beat forecasts. INFERENCE: The 1m bear-flattening is the market's slowdown tax on a hike that was already in the price. If growth and risk appetite remain resilient, 2s should stop cheapening versus 10s: either the additional-hike premium in 2s fades now that September is delivered, or term yields stay bid with activity and the curve re-steepens. The desk line that domestic growth is softer is the over-discounted pessimism. UNKNOWN: Next-meeting hike odds are not in the packet; positioning/flow is unavailable; NZ yields are blocked so NZ growth cannot be expressed in rates; 5y 2s10s percentile is 54%, so the flattening is extreme only on the 1y window.
why_now: The Sep 16 hike is done and had been greater than 90% priced, so further flattening now has to come from a genuine growth scare rather than from delivering a known FOMC outcome.
US 2s10s just printed the 0th percentile of the 252-observation opportunity screen and 1y percentile 0.2% after a statistically large 1m flatten.
Same-week triangulation is still expansionary: ISM Services 55.4, August retail +1.2%, payrolls +162k, VIX 15.44, HY OAS 270bp, copper at the 92nd percentile.
Canada and NZ growth prints (CA GDP +0.8% q/q; NZ GDP beat at +0.2% q/q) argue the global cyclical complex is not rolling over even as the desk narrative leans softer growth.
Saudi ship-to-ship workaround and modest oil easing reduce the extreme left tail that would justify a lasting curve collapse, even though energy shock absorbers remain a risk.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Own the post-FOMC USD tightening premium against AUD, the G10 USD pair that has not yet paid for Australian housing damage and delivered US policy.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Australian housing/labor confirmation plus a still-intact Fed tightening path while AUDUSD catches down to other USD pairs.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: US tightening bias withdrawn or Australian housing/labor re-acceleration restoring AUD relative-rate support.

contribution.stance_summary: USD is the clean benchmark: post-FOMC tightening bias plus broadening G10 tightening should be owned in USD spot, not in a cross. AUDUSD is the laggard USD pair—Australian housing is already breaking while AUD has not paid the USD premium already visible versus EUR, GBP, NZD and CAD.

catalysts: Further Australian housing, transaction, and labor prints confirming the tightening channel is still biting.
US inflation and Fed communication that keep the post-hike tightening bias intact rather than one-and-done.
Continued G10 tightening impulse (BoJ follow-through, BoE hawkish dissent/QT) that sustains the USD policy premium AUD has not paid.
AUDUSD catch-down toward the 1m USD moves already printed in EURUSD, GBPUSD, NZDUSD and USDCAD.
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk

expression_comparison.rationale: Dedicated USD-spot seat. The discrepancy is that AUDUSD has not repriced the delivered USD policy premium and the Australian housing/tightening-channel break; that lives in the USD pair. A rates sleeve (US outright duration or AU-US 2Y RV) owns yield levels that are already historically extreme and does not harvest the FX lag. A cross such as AUDCAD adds CAD oil, BoC energy-pass-through and stronger Canadian activity as second-order risk on an Australia-versus-USD view.

trade.invalidation: Thesis fails if AUDUSD resumes higher because US inflation/labor temperatures roll over and the Fed tightening bias is withdrawn, or if Australian housing and labor evidence reverse into a re-acceleration that restores RBA hawkish relative-rate support versus the US. Wrong-timing, not wrong-thesis, if global USD bid pauses but AU housing physicals and US policy bias remain intact.
trade.mispricing: AUDUSD still trades as if Australian financial-conditions damage and the delivered USD tightening premium were comparable to a flat 1m outcome. The pair remains statistically rich (5y 84th percentile) while US front-end yields have already repriced hard and other USD pairs have already moved. The 2Y sovereign differential only mildly favors AUD (about +26bp, carry ratio 0.049) so the FX lag is not explained by a large AUD carry cushion; it is unexplained residual USD-underpricing versus AUD.
principal_risks: FOMC was already >90% priced; buying USD solely on the hike is stale unless the path and the AUD lag remain the live gap.
AU 2Y 4.999% versus US 2Y 4.76% and AU 10Y 5.348% versus US 10Y 5.01% mean rate differentials do not independently favor short AUDUSD; a relative AU hawkish re-steepening would squeeze the short.
AUD commodity/terms-of-trade beta into the energy shock is not quantified here and can bid AUD independently of housing.
US consumer temperature 48.5 with weaker confidence is a USD-negative tail if it ends the Fed tightening bias.
Positioning/flow is unavailable; crowded USD-long or AUD-short ownership cannot be tested.
No executable broker prices; research/reference ECB fixes cannot be used as entries, targets or stops.
trade.thesis: FACT: The Fed delivered a 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% after August CPI kept the tightening bias intact; rate futures had already assigned greater-than-90% odds to that 25bp step, so the decision itself is largely known information. FACT: US 2Y is 4.76% (1y z 2.84, +57bp over 1m) and US 10Y is 5.01%; the desk thesis is that BoJ’s hike to 1.25% and the BoE’s 6–3 hold with three hike votes broaden global tightening and that the energy shock is constraining the G10 easing impulse. FACT: Australian housing is showing the tightening channel in physical data—NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y, transactions -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak—while AU labor 47.8 and activity 49.2 sit at or below the US analogs (labor 50.2, activity 49.92). FACT: AUDUSD research/reference fix 0.712 is still in the 84th 5y percentile (z 1.23) with a 1m return of only +0.20%, versus EURUSD -1.89%, GBPUSD -2.07%, NZDUSD -3.90% and USDCAD +1.74% over the same window. INFERENCE: The USD policy premium is being paid in other G10 USD pairs; AUD is the residual, so the clean USD-spot expression is short AUDUSD rather than chasing already-extended USDCAD or already-washed NZDUSD. INFERENCE: Cross-short AUDCAD (5y z 2.76, 99.96th percentile) mixes a valid AUD-rich observation with an implicit CAD long that imports oil, BoC energy-pass-through and Canada’s stronger activity (53.2) and consumer (52.5) temperatures—unnecessary second-order risk. UNKNOWN: Cot/positioning is unavailable; executable broker levels are not in the packet; NZ official yields are unavailable so NZD relative-rate RV cannot be completed; whether AUD’s commodity beta offsets housing stress is not identified in this freeze.
why_now: The FOMC hike is now realized, not just >90% priced, and August CPI left the Fed tightening bias intact—known decision, still-live path.
Last-24 desk thesis: BoJ 25bp to 1.25% and BoE 6–3 hold broaden tightening and keep term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer; that is new transmission after the Fed print.
Australian housing physicals (stamp duty, volumes, home values) document the RBA tightening channel while AUDUSD has not sold off with the rest of the USD complex.
US 2Y +57bp over 1m versus AUDUSD +0.20% 1m is the live level-versus-change gap; 5d AUDUSD -0.73% is only the start of catch-down.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Australian housing and labor are already breaking under higher rates, so AU 2Y at a 5-year extreme still prices too much further RBA tightening while risk assets remain complacent.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Next Australian housing/labor/RBA signal that the tightening channel is still contracting.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Housing/labor stabilize or energy pass-through forces another RBA hike that lifts AU 2Y.

contribution.stance_summary: Global tightening is being piled into an energy shock while Australian housing and labor are already breaking; markets still price AU 2Y as if more RBA restraint is required, and risk assets remain complacent. The cleanest slowdown expression is receive AU 2Y duration, not chasing already-extended AUD spot.

catalysts: Further Australian housing, employment, or activity prints confirming the tightening channel is still contracting.
RBA communication that the housing/labor deterioration constrains further tightening despite the global energy overlay.
Risk-off transmission from still-complacent equity/credit/vol into G10 duration if the energy shock and broader tightening stay live.
evidence_refs: rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Receive Australian 2-year government bonds (outright long front-end duration on RBA F2 2Y; research/reference yields only).
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates is the cleaner owner of the discrepancy: AU 2Y sits at a 99th-percentile 1y and 5y stretch while the housing-credit channel is already contracting, so the mispricing is the RBA path not the FX level. Spot AUDUSD is only 84th percentile 5y and already cheap vs copper on the packet residual, so a short is less aligned with where the gap lives. AUDCAD is more statistically extreme but mixes a 165bp AUD-over-CAD carry headwind with Canada energy support, so it is a dirtier slowdown expression. NZ rates RV is unavailable (official B2 403). Curve steepener (receive 2s/pay 10s) is a valid hedge against the desk's term-premium overlay but AU 2s10s is only about the 24th percentile 1y and is not where the stretch or the housing mechanism sits; 2Y tenor owns the policy path and is less exposed to energy-driven term premium than 10Y. Mandate prefers rates when comparably clean; here rates is superior, not merely default.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDUSD (fade still-elevated AUD vs USD as housing/labor slowdown and global tightening hit the cycle currency).

trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if Australian housing volumes/prices stabilize and AU labor/activity reheat, or if energy pass-through / an RBA hike lifts AU 2Y as a continued tightening cycle rather than a growth break. Timing is merely delayed if 2Y stays high while housing/labor keep deteriorating.
trade.mispricing: AU 2Y at the 99th percentile 1y and 5y still embeds further RBA tightening after the housing channel has already broken (stamp duty -24%, volumes -18%, prices more than 7% off peak) and labor is loosening. Pricing requires housing/labor to re-accelerate or energy to reopen an AU inflation impulse; the packet's domestic gauges do not show that.
principal_risks: Desk-thesis risk: energy shock keeps front-end yields rising even where domestic growth is softer, so receive-AU-2Y is fighting global tightening rather than owning a local pause.
Energy pass-through into AU inflation (trimmed mean still 3.6%) forces the RBA to hike into housing weakness (policy-error continuation, not pivot).
Saudi Oman crude workaround already reduced the extreme oil-supply tail, allowing a growth re-acceleration and bond selloff if energy fades.
No positioning/flow dataset: the AU 2Y extreme could already be owned, and executable levels are absent so sizing/entry cannot be priced from this packet.
trade.structure: Outright receive AU 2Y government bonds / long front-end duration. Packet yields are RBA F2 research/reference closes, not executable broker prices.
trade.thesis: FACT: NSW stamp-duty receipts fell 24% y/y in August with transaction volumes -18% and Sydney/Melbourne home values more than 7% below peak; AU labor temperature is 47.8 (unemployment 4.5% from 4.4%, employment -15.8k m/m, WPI +3.2% y/y vs +3.4%); AU activity 49.2 with business conditions/confidence soft; headline CPI eased to 3.5% y/y while trimmed mean held 3.6%. FACT: AU 2Y yield is 4.999% as of 2026-09-16, 99.0th percentile 1y and 99.8th percentile 5y, +39bp 1m / +50bp 3m. FACT: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% with August CPI keeping a tightening bias; BoJ hiked to 1.25%; BoE held 3.75% but a 6-3 split with three members preferring a hike plus gilt QT; desk thesis is that the energy shock is constraining global easing and keeping term-rate pressure elevated even where growth is softer. FACT: SPX near the 90th percentile, VIX 15.44 near the 15th percentile, HY OAS 270bp near the 14th percentile, while Brent is 130.8 (near the 99.6th) and WTI 107 (near the 96th). INFERENCE: The tightening channel is already delivering an Australian housing/labor slowdown, so AU 2Y at a 5-year extreme is pricing additional RBA restraint that the domestic data cannot support; the global energy/tightening overlay is why duration has not rallied, which is the mispricing rather than a reason to pay more. 2Y is the correct tenor because it owns the RBA path; 10Y is contaminated by the same term-premium shock the desk flags. INFERENCE: Risk markets have not priced this cluster (complacent vol/credit vs energy and G10 tightening), so the growth-break remains available in rates. UNKNOWN: positioning/flow; executable AU bond prices; whether energy pass-through hits AU CPI next; RBNZ yields (official source blocked); whether the Saudi Oman workaround has already capped the oil tail.
why_now: Sep 16 housing evidence shows the RBA tightening channel biting in real time (stamp duty, volumes, peak-to-trough prices) while AU 2Y remains at a 5-year extreme.

Sep 16-18 policy cluster (Fed hike, BoJ hike, BoE 6-3 hold with QT) is the overlay keeping global duration offered; that is new information relative to a local AU housing break and is why 2Y has not yet priced the slowdown.

Risk pricing is still complacent (VIX near the 15th percentile, HY OAS near the 14th, SPX near the 90th) against Brent/WTI at 1y extremes, so the defensive repricing has not happened in beta and remains available in AU front-end rates.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: US front-end cheapening continues because price, Fed/G10 policy and inflation revisions are aligned; stretch is not a reversal.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Post-Fed/BoJ/BoE-dissent tightening impulse plus energy shock keeping the easing path closed
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: US 2Y reverses the sourced one-month +57bp uptrend without a new hawkish policy or inflation impulse
conflict_synopsis.primary_trade: Pay/short US 2Y duration; reject fading the 100th-percentile front-end yield
conflict_synopsis.time_horizon: 2-8 weeks, through the next US inflation/labor prints and any BoC energy pass-through test

contribution.stance_summary: Pay US 2Y duration. Price, policy and revisions are aligned for higher US front-end yields; fading the 100th-percentile print is premature without a reversal signal. Long USDCAD is the concrete spot continuation but is inferior to owning the rates trend directly.

catalysts: Follow-through from the Fed hike and August CPI tightening bias into subsequent US inflation and labor prints.
Persistence of the energy shock and weaker shock absorbers keeping term-rate pressure elevated.
Global tightening confirmation via BoJ 1.25% and BoE dissent/QT rather than a dovish hold.
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Pay/short US 2Y outright duration (UST 2-year notes). Sourced US 2Y is 4.76% as of 2026-09-18 with +9bp 1d, +13bp 5d and +57bp 1m/3m; opportunity-monitor z 2.89 and 100th percentile. Continuation of the front-end sell-off after the Fed hike, not a 2s10s flattener (term-premium pressure can lift the long end) and not CA-US RV (that spread is already the US-outperformance trend, but BoC energy catch-up is a two-sided residual).
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates are preferred because they are comparably clean and own the discrepancy more directly. Verified: desk thesis and BoJ last24 both locate the Tier-1 transmission in global duration and term-rate pricing, not FX; US 2Y has same-day official history (age_days 0) with a 1-month move z 3.29; USDCAD versus CA-US 2Y is a weak residual (r-squared 0.022). Inference: fading a 100th-percentile yield because it is stretched is a mean-reversion prior, not a reversal signal. Spot USDCAD is a valid but second-best expression of the same tightening gap. expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long USDCAD. Sourced spot 1.4010 as of 2026-09-18, +0.11% 1d, +1.10% 5d, +1.74% 1m, 87th percentile 5y; 2Y yield differential +140bp USD over CAD. Same Fed-BoC policy-gap continuation.

trade.horizon: 2-8 weeks, through the next US inflation/labor prints and any BoC energy pass-through test
trade.invalidation: A multi-session US 2Y reversal that erases the sourced one-month +57bp rise without a new hawkish policy or inflation impulse; or a documented G10 easing pivot that reopens the cut path the desk thesis says is constrained.
trade.mispricing: The live discrepancy is not that US 2Y is 'too high' versus its 252-observation distribution. Research method: statistical stretch is a yardstick, not a fade signal. The market still treats the post-hike, post-CPI, post-BoJ/BoE-dissent complex as fadeable because the hike was >90% priced and the 2Y sits at the 100th percentile. What is under-owned is persistence: energy-constrained easing plus a broadening G10 tightening impulse that keeps the front-end cheapening after the decision. Expressing that in US 2Y owns the tenor where the 1-month move is largest and freshest.
principal_risks: Negative carry from paying 2Y while waiting; a growth scare that bull-steepens without a policy reversal still hurts a short 2Y.
Saudi Oman ship-to-ship crude and any further energy workaround could trim the inflation tail the desk is using to block easing.
US consumer 48.5 and activity 49.92 are already slightly cool; a sharp labor break would be the first real fade catalyst.
No positioning dataset and no executable broker prices; size and levels cannot be refined from this packet.
CA 1d yield decline and AU 1d dip show local mean-reversion noise that could temporarily pull US fronts if risk-on duration demand returns.
trade.structure: Outright pay-fixed / short US 2Y duration; cash or futures equivalent. Not a curve flattener and not a CA-US basis.
trade.thesis: Verified fact: the Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep after futures were already >90% priced for the hike; August CPI kept the tightening bias intact; US 2Y then printed 4.76% on 18 Sep with +9bp on the day and +57bp over one month (move z 3.29, level z 2.89, 100th percentile). The same window shows US 5Y +51bp 1m and US 10Y +36bp 1m, so the front end is leading. BoJ hiked to 1.25% (7-2) and BoE held 3.75% 6-3 with three votes for 4.00% plus a multi-year gilt unwind; the last-24 desk thesis states the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse and keeping term-rate pressure elevated. US inflation temperature is 52.0. Inference: price trend, policy impulse and inflation revision are aligned, so the 2Y uptrend persists longer than a fade of the percentile stretch implies. A 2s10s flattener is the wrong rates expression: 2s10s is already 25bp (0th percentile, -21bp 1m) while BoE QT and the desk's term-premium language can lift the long end even as the front stays bid to cheapen. CA-US 2Y at -140bp and CA-US 5Y at -124bp (0th percentile, -17bp/-16bp 1m) confirm US outperformance versus Canada, but that RV imports BoC energy-pass-through catch-up risk without improving ownership of the US policy path. Spot long USDCAD is the same gap in FX and is retained only as the comparison candidate. Unknown: positioning/flow is unavailable; NZ official yields are unavailable and unused; no executable entry exists in the packet. Saudi ship-to-ship crude is a tail-risk reducer, not a documented reversal of the tightening impulse.
why_now: US 2Y as of 2026-09-18 is still rising after the 16 Sep hike (+9bp 1d, +13bp 5d, +57bp 1m), so the post-decision fade has not started.
BoJ hike to 1.25% and BoE 6-3 hold with three hike votes arrived after the Fed print and keep the global tightening impulse live into this cutoff.
Energy-shock-absorber weakening and BoC pass-through risk remain open; they constrain easing more than they justify buying duration at a 100th-percentile yield.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: AUDNZD's 5y extreme is a two-way event-risk discrepancy that a bounded put spread owns better than spot or blocked AU-NZ rates RV.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: AU housing/labor evidence that the tightening channel is biting while NZD stops cheapening through otherwise constructive NZ news.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AUDNZD makes a new extreme as AU housing stabilizes and NZ labor/activity stay NZD-negative, or live implied vol already prices the unwind versus 20d realized.
conflict_synopsis.primary_trade: short AUDNZD via 1-3m defined-risk put spread

own_original.stance_summary: AUDNZD is the packet's most stretched G10 cross (5y 99.96th percentile, z 3.12) after a 4.27% one-month rise, while NZ 2Y yields and therefore AU-NZ rate RV and AUDNZD carry are unavailable. Spot shorting the cross is the wrong instrument: timing of mean reversion is unknown, NZD already has two-way event risk (Q2 GDP beat and India trade deal versus 5.6% unemployment), and a spot short has unbounded continuation risk. Own the reversal with a defined-risk 1-3m AUDNZD put spread. Implied vol, skew and strikes are not in the packet and remain unquoted; do not execute until a live screen shows the premium is not already pricing the unwind versus 20d realized 5.09%.

catalysts: Further evidence that the RBA tightening channel is biting (housing volumes, stamp duty, AU labor) without a matching NZD-negative growth miss.
NZ data or RBNZ communication that re-anchors NZD after the Q2 GDP beat and India trade implementation, reversing the 1m NZDUSD slide that built the cross extreme.
Energy/G10 tightening event risk that lifts FX implied from a still-unobserved base; only then is vol itself the P&L, and only if the live screen confirms it was not already priced.
evidence_refs: rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
rollup:New Zealand Q2 GDP slows to 0.2% q/q but beats forecasts

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: AU 10Y outright (5.348, 1y 99th percentile as of 2026-09-16) or AU-NZ 2Y RV; the NZ leg is not executable because official NZ sovereign yields are unavailable (HTTP 403) and AUDNZD vs AU-NZ 2Y is status insufficient.
expression_comparison.rationale: The discrepancy lives in the AUDNZD distribution and in two-way NZ/AU event risk, not in a clean AU duration or AU-NZ curve view. Rates cannot own the NZ side: rates:NZ is unavailable and xa:opportunities marks AUDNZD carry and AUDNZD~AU-NZ_2Y as unavailable/insufficient. Spot short AUDNZD fights an unknown carry and has unbounded risk if NZD labor weakness (unemployment 5.6%) extends the 1m -3.90% NZDUSD slide. A 1-3m put spread bounds premium, keeps the short-AUD/long-NZD delta, and does not require inventing a reversion clock. Do not substitute an AUDUSD or AUDCAD spot short: AUDUSD is only 84th percentile and has lagged copper (residual z -1.33); AUDCAD is also 99.96th percentile but 2Y carry of 165bp / 60d vol 4.93 explicitly compensates a spot fade, whereas AUDNZD carry cannot even be measured.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDNZD cash at ECB reference 1.2468 (research/reference only, not executable).

trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if AUDNZD extends to a new extreme while AU housing/labor stop deteriorating and NZ activity/inflation fail to support NZD, or if a live broker screen shows AUDNZD implied vol and 25d risk-reversal already fully pricing the unwind versus sourced 20d realized 5.09% (AUDNZD) and 6.31% (NZDUSD). Right-thesis/wrong-timing if the mechanism is intact but the option decays through the 1-3m window without a catalyst; reassess rather than rolling into spot.
trade.mispricing: Market pricing in the frozen packet is the AUDNZD level itself at a 5y extreme (percentile 99.96, z 3.12) after NZDUSD sold 3.90% in a month through a GDP beat and a trade-deal headline, while AU housing and AU labor are already showing the tightening channel. That is a fundamentals-versus-distribution and market-versus-market discrepancy (AUDUSD not equivalently stretched; AUDUSD vs copper residual z -1.33). It is not an implied-versus-realized claim: FX implied vol and skew are missing. Do not treat the z-score as a mean-reversion signal; it is the historical reference that makes a bounded option the cleaner way to wait for a catalyst.
principal_risks: NZD labor is the weakest of the four (unemployment 5.6%); a spot-like continuation in NZDUSD can grind through a put spread if implied was not cheap.
Implied vol, skew and fly are unknown; the structure can be a negative-carry debit if AUDNZD implied is already rich to 20d realized 5.09%.
AUDNZD carry cannot be measured; if the missing NZ 2Y later shows a large AUD yield advantage, theta works against the short cross.
No positioning/flow dataset: a crowded NZD short squeeze or AUD long liquidation cannot be distinguished from macro.
Global energy shock and higher-for-longer US yields can hit NZD as the higher-RV, weaker-percentile currency, extending AUDNZD.
ECB FX prints are research/reference only; executable spot and option markets can differ.
trade.structure: Defined-risk 1-3 month AUDNZD put spread: buy a closer-to-spot AUDNZD put, sell a further out-of-the-money put. Equivalent delta is short AUD / long NZD with known debit. No strike, delta, premium, implied vol or risk-reversal quote is sourced in this packet; those must be taken from a live broker screen before execution. If 25d risk-reversal already prices NZD upside versus 20d realized 5.09% (AUDNZD) and 6.31% (NZDUSD), shrink size or stand down rather than inventing a cheapness claim.
trade.thesis: FACT: On 2026-09-18 ECB same-fixing research crosses, AUDNZD spot is 1.2468, 5y percentile 99.96, z 3.12, 1m return +4.27%, 20d realized vol 5.09%. The same snapshot has NZDUSD at 0.5711, 5y percentile 8.61, z -1.15, 1m -3.90%, 20d RV 6.31%, versus AUDUSD 0.7120, 5y percentile 84.3, z 1.23, 1m only +0.20%, 20d RV 4.71%. So the cross extreme is mostly NZD underperformance, not an AUD melt-up. AU 10Y is 5.348 (1y percentile 99.0, 1m +26bp) with NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y and Sydney/Melbourne home values more than 7% off peak; AU labor temperature is 47.8 (unemployment 4.5%, employment -15.8k m/m). NZ Q2 GDP printed +0.2% q/q but beat forecasts; NZ inflation temperature is 51.6; NZ labor is 47.0 with unemployment 5.6%; parliament passed an India trade deal covering about 95% of NZ exports to India. Official NZ yields are unavailable, so AUDNZD carry and AU-NZ 2Y RV are not in the packet. Equity VIX is 15.44 (percentile 14.7, z -0.84) while Brent is 130.8 (percentile 99.6) and WTI 107.02 (percentile 96.4); USDJPY 20d RV is 11.04 after a +1.41% 1d rally on the BoJ hike to 1.25%. Positioning/flow is unavailable. Executable option prices are not in the packet. INFERENCE: Spot is the wrong expression because the closing mechanism (AU housing/labor biting versus a sold-off NZD that just beat GDP) has unknown timing and two-way event risk; a cash short is an unbounded bet that NZD cannot cheapen further, and a cash long is buying a 5y extreme. The put spread owns the same AUD-down/NZD-up discrepancy with defined debit. Cross-asset, suppressed VIX against an energy and G10-tightening regime is a reason to worry that event risk is underpriced in vol markets we can observe, but that is equity vol not AUDNZD implied and is not a substitute for a live FX vol screen. UNKNOWN: AUDNZD implied vol, 25d risk reversal, fly, forward points, and NZ 2Y. Cot/positioning. Whether the NZD slide is flow/liquidation rather than macro (no plumbing dataset).
why_now: AUDNZD prints the packet's most extreme G10 FX percentile (99.96) and z (3.12) on the 2026-09-18 snapshot, with the 1m move already +4.27%.

The Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% was >90% priced and is now known information; the live relative impulse is AU housing/labor versus a NZD that cheapened through a Q2 GDP beat and the India trade law — a two-way event window, not a drift that spot can sit on.
AU-NZ rate RV and AUDNZD carry remain untradeable while NZ yields stay unavailable, so waiting for a rates expression abandons the FX discrepancy.

VIX at 15.44 (14.7th percentile) versus Brent at the 99.6th percentile and USDJPY 20d RV 11% is the observable vol-regime warning; FX implied is still unchecked and must be checked before paying premium.
